editorial:
Imagine it is the summer of 1984, and you are hanging out with your best friends in a small town where everyone knows everyone. You probably think the scariest thing in town is a local legend, but for Timmy, Barry, and Doug, those stories start feeling way too real. After a teenage couple vanishes near the local graveyard, these three kids decide to investigate. It feels a lot like Stand by Me, but with a creepy twist. You get to follow these three damaged kids as they try to figure out if a real monster is living under the dirt or if something even worse is going on in their neighborhood.

What really makes this work is the acting, especially from Nolan Gould, who brings a lot of heart to the role. The movie does a great job of making you feel the tension as the boys get closer to the truth. While the budget is small and some of the effects look a bit dated, the story keeps you hooked. If you love spooky mysteries, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, the boys discover that the Ghoul is a real, flesh-eating monster living in the cemetery. After a scary showdown, they realize the monster was lured there by the town's dark secrets. Timmy and his friends manage to survive the encounter, but they are forever changed. They learn that the real monsters are sometimes the people living right next door, and they leave their childhood innocence behind to survive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s nostalgia and creepy creature features.
